concepts.def: Manufacture of a single unique product, used for bespoke commissions; labour-intensive but flexible.
Manufacture of a limited quantity of identical products before retooling for the next batch, balancing flexibility and efficiency.
Continuous large-scale manufacture of standardised products, pioneered for cars by Henry Ford's Model T line in 1913.
Production system minimising stock by delivering components as needed, developed by Toyota in the 1970s.
Manufacturing running 24/7 to produce uninterrupted output, used in industries such as glass, chemicals and electricity generation.
Manufacturing organisation grouping equipment into cells where teams complete identifiable units, improving flexibility and morale.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Manufacturing Processes & Techniques — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Manufacturing Processes & Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Manufacturing Processes & Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In what year did Ford introduce the moving assembly line for the Model T?
Which company developed the just-in-time manufacturing system?
options: Ford
Toyota
General Motors
Honda

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
It is the cheapest method for any quantity.
It is the only way to make plastic items.
Tooling cost is high but per-unit cost is very low at scale.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: It is the only way to make plastic items.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
They are the same thing with different names.

mcqs.q: Which of the 6 Rs has the GREATEST environmental benefit?
options: Recycle (because it is most familiar).
Refuse or Reduce (preventing the impact at source).
Repair (because it sounds eco-friendly).
It is the only way to make plastic items.
